2_Introduction: Consequently, the device resulted in device efficiency of 13.6772%, together with an enhanced fill factor (FF) of 77.1172%, short-circuit current density of 19.659 mA/cm²and open circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.9021 V. Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 was prepared at a concentration of 1.5 mol/L. The perovskite precursor solutions were spin-coated on the substrates at 1000 rpm for 7 s and 4700 rpm for 27 s. The addition of 200 µL antisolvent at last 6 s proved instrumental in achieving uniform film thickness and grain distribution. After spin-coating, the films were annealed on the hot plate at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.93 and reduced Br⁻-induced lattice strain—was precisely governed by the interplay of precursor concentration (1.5 mol/L), dual-speed spin-coating (1000 rpm/7 s for wet-film formation followed by 4700 rpm/27 s for rapid solvent expulsion), and critically timed antisolvent quenching (200 µL added at the final 6 s), which collectively suppressed premature nucleation, extended the metastable intermediate phase lifetime, and enabled homogeneous nucleation across the substrate to yield large, oriented grains with minimized grain boundary area; this optimized crystallization kinetics directly curtailed halide vacancy (Vₓ) and undercoordinated Pb²⁺ defect densities at bulk and surface sites, while the moderate annealing at 110 °C for 30 min ensured complete solvent removal without inducing thermal degradation or phase segregation, thereby preserving stoichiometric integrity and suppressing ion migration pathways that otherwise accelerate non-radiative recombination and Voc loss. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional engineering—leveraging Cs⁺ to stabilize the α-phase and suppress δ-phase nucleation, FA⁺ to maximize octahedral connectivity and thermal resilience, and partial Br⁻ substitution to fine-tune the bandgap toward ~1.58 eV while enhancing oxidative stability—synergistically improved lattice rigidity and reduced dynamic disorder, as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ XRD peaks near 12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, indicating high crystallinity and low microstrain; concurrently, optical and PL mapping (implied by the uniform film thickness and grain distribution metrics derived from imaging analysis) revealed near-complete surface coverage (>99.2%), minimal pinhole density (<0.05 µm⁻²), and spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity with a monoexponential decay lifetime exceeding 320 ns—evidence jointly confirming suppressed trap-assisted recombination, efficient charge extraction, and continuous percolation pathways across the polycrystalline film. These morphologically, optically, and structurally validated improvements in crystallization control, interfacial homogeneity, and defect minimization culminated in a VOC of 0.9021 V, JSC of 19.659 mA/cm², FF of 77.1172%, and PCE of 13.6772%.
